validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #108 collects nine follow-up findings the review and QA of PR #100 left open, all landing in packages/loot-core/src/shared/transactions.ts — the module that reduces split parents and their children into the flat rows the register holds. I re-drove the load-bearing ones myself against current main with a scratch vitest file in the loot-core workspace (removed afterwards; nothing committed, nothing left on disk). F1, F2, F3 and F4 all reproduce with the exact wrong values the review reported: deleting every leg of an opened split collapses it to a row at the right amount with `payee: null`; unsplitting a split whose first leg was cleared to null yields a survivor at the right amount with `payee: null`; and a parent that survives a partial unsplit keeps a `SplitTransactionError` whose `difference` (12345) no longer matches its new amount (7345). F7, which claims the `?? parent.payee` half is dead code and asks for `payee: data.payee ?? null`, is FALSE and applying it would be a regression: on the #8207 conversion path the new split parent is built by spreading `...transaction` over the plain row and so keeps its payee, and I confirmed the survivor on that shape returns `payee-original` today purely through that fallback. I also confirmed a second live path (editing a split parent's payee leaves it non-null). F5 (files PR #100 touched that its work order did not name) and F9 (the previous order's AC-13 verification step is not performable as written) are notes about a merged plan rather than defects in code; F8 folds into F3's test. What ships is three behaviour changes in one function and its one sibling, the tests that can fail without them, and the release note the repository's gate requires.
validated_work_order.root_cause: `splitTransaction` (transactions.ts:414-423) moves a split's payee down onto the children by building the parent with `payee: null`. Three places then build a row out of that parent and inherit the null or the parent's pre-unsplit error, each fixed by hand at the time and therefore inconsistent with the others: (1) `deleteTransaction`'s `subtransactions?.length === 1` collapse (:377-386) spreads the parent and overrides only `is_parent` and `error`, so the survivor loses the payee — the identical shape PR #100 repaired in `makeTransactionWithChildCategory`, one function over, which is why the review calls it the same defect surviving on the sibling site; (2) `makeTransactionWithChildCategory`'s `payee: data.payee ?? parent.payee` (:129) reads only the FIRST promoted row, and `??` treats an explicit null as absent, so a first leg the user deliberately cleared falls through to a parent that is itself null; (3) the surviving-parent branch (:549-554) changes the parent's `amount` but spreads `error` from `parentTransaction`, which was measured against the pre-unsplit children, so the 'Amount left:' banner renders a figure that disagrees with the row and a Distribute button wired to it. The shared rule is: a row rebuilt from a split must take its identity and its figures from the split's own children, not from the parent.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three behaviour edits in `transactions.ts`, then the tests that must go red without them.

1. Payee on the delete-collapse (`:377-386`). The branch already holds the leg it is collapsing onto — `trans.subtransactions[0]` — so read the payee off it: `payee: trans.subtransactions[0].payee ?? rest.payee`. `??` is right rather than a 'first non-null' scan because there is exactly one leg here. `rest.payee` (the parent's) is the correct fallback for the shapes where a split parent still carries a payee.

2. Payee on the promoted row (`makeTransactionWithChildCategory`, `:110-131` and its two call sites at `:471` and `:530`). This is the real defect; F7's remedy is wrong. Keep the parent fallback and change which row it reads: resolve the payee at the caller as the first promoted row that actually carries one, falling back to the parent's. The caller already computes `newNonChildTransactions`. I checked this rule against all five reachable shapes — the four existing payee cases keep their exact current values and only the cleared-leg shape changes (`null` -> the other leg's payee). It must NOT become `payee: data.payee ?? null`: that turns the #8207 shape's correct `payee-original` into `null`, reintroducing the bug this class of work exists to close.

3. Error on the surviving parent (`:549-554`). The amount already moves; the error must be re-measured against the children that REMAIN behind the parent (`remainingChildTransactions`, already in scope). The obvious remedy — handing `updatedParentTransaction` to the existing `recalculateSplit` — is wrong, and I confirmed why: in this branch `parentTransaction` carries no `subtransactions` at all, so the helper measures against zero and reports 7345 where the truth is 500 on a 12345/5000/4345/2500 split. But the helper is reusable if it is handed the remaining children rather than the parent's stale ones: `recalculateSplit({ ...parentTransaction, amount: <newAmount>, subtransactions: remainingChildTransactions }).error` returns 500 on that fixture, `null` when the remainder balances the new amount, 7345 on the all-zero-remainder fixture, and `null` on a balanced negative expense — identical to computing the difference by hand. Prefer that over widening `SplitTransactionError`: it reuses the existing rule (balanced means no error) instead of restating it, keeps the `type`/`version` in one place, and changes no shared signature.

4. Comment. The block above the payee line is being rewritten anyway because the expression under it changes, so it must end up describing the code as it now is — in particular it must not keep the claim that the parent's payee is null on every path, which this work disproves. No target length is specified; see `out_of_scope`.

Tests, one per branch, each required to have been seen red with its fix reverted (conventions.md, and the reason this suite's tests did not catch the original bug). Delete-collapse: open a real split, delete one leg then the other, assert the collapsed row carries the leg's payee. Cleared-leg: a split whose first leg is `payee: null` and whose second carries one, assert the survivor still carries it. Parent-fallback: the #8207 shape, pinned so F7 can never be re-applied. Keep-parent: unsplit one leg of a three-child split and assert both the promoted leg's payee and the parent's corrected `error` — balanced -> `null`, shortfall -> the true remainder. That last case is F3 and F8 together, and the three-child fixture is the one the existing payee cases never exercise.

files.change: Three behaviour edits plus a comment correction. (a) `deleteTransaction`'s `subtransactions?.length === 1` collapse (:377-386) gains `payee: trans.subtransactions[0].payee ?? rest.payee` beside its existing `is_parent: false` and `error: null` overrides. (b) `makeTransactionWithChildCategory` (:110-131) stops taking the payee off the passed row and the two call sites (:471 single-child early return, :530 keep-parent branch) resolve it as the first promoted row carrying one, falling back to the parent's — the `?? parent.payee` fallback STAYS, because F7's claim that it is dead code is disproven on the #8207 conversion path and on a split parent whose payee was edited. (c) The surviving-parent branch (:549-554) sets `error` from `recalculateSplit` applied to the parent at its NEW amount with `subtransactions: remainingChildTransactions`, so the figure measures the children that remain rather than the parent's pre-unsplit set. No signature changes. (d) The comment block at :118-128 is rewritten to describe the expression as it now reads, including that a split parent does NOT always have a null payee.
files.why: Every confirmed behaviour defect in this ticket is in this one file, and edit (c) is only possible here because `remainingChildTransactions` is already in scope at the surviving-parent branch.

files.change: Add four cases beside the existing payee block (:950-1083): one driving the real `deleteTransaction` through a two-leg delete to the collapse and asserting the survivor's payee; one for a first leg explicitly cleared to null where a later leg carries a payee; one pinning the #8207 parent-fallback shape so the fallback cannot be removed; and one on the keep-parent branch built from a three-child `makeOpenedSplit`, asserting the promoted leg's payee and the parent's corrected `error` (balanced -> null, shortfall -> the true remainder, which must also go red against the naive `recalculateSplit(updatedParentTransaction)` remedy). Each new case must be recorded failing with its fix reverted.
files.why: F3 asks for a payee assertion on the keep-parent branch and F8 asks for the multi-child fixture; F8 itself says the two are the same test. F1, F2 and edit (c) each ship a behaviour change to money-touching code and each needs a case able to fail.

files.change: One-line `Bugfixes` note covering the user-visible half: a transaction that stops being a split no longer loses its payee when a leg is deleted or unsplit, and the 'Amount left:' figure on a partially unsplit split now matches the row. `authors` must be a real GitHub username — the gate's identity denylist rejects `claude` and `github-actions` — so the implementer sets it from the committing account.

Browser confirmation: open a 123.45 transaction under a payee you choose, Split it into 50.00 and 73.45, save, select both legs and delete them; the register shows one 123.45 row under that payee, not a blank one.

acceptance.check: Unsplitting a split whose first leg's payee was deliberately cleared yields a surviving row carrying another leg's payee, not `payee: null`.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The second new case. Browser confirmation: open a 123.45 transaction under a payee, Split it, clear the first leg's payee field, save, unsplit both legs — the survivor carries the payee of the leg that has one, and the register's payee search finds it.

acceptance.check: The parent-payee fallback stays: on a split parent that still carries a non-null payee — reachable when `updateTransaction` promotes a plain transaction into a split via `subtransactions`, and when a split parent's payee is edited — the survivor inherits it instead of becoming payee-less.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The third new case. This is the finding F7 asked to delete; it must survive the change. Written as its own case so a future reader cannot re-derive F7's conclusion from the code and 'fix' it again — which would be a regression, not a cleanup.

qa_script: AC-1: open a 123.45 transaction under a named payee, Split into 50.00 + 73.45, save, select both legs, delete both. Expect ONE 123.45 row still under that payee, not a blank one.

AC-2: open a 123.45 transaction under a named payee, Split, clear the first leg's payee, save, unsplit both legs. Expect the survivor under the other leg's payee; then search the register for that payee and expect the row in the result set.

AC-4: open a 123.45 transaction, Split into 50.00 / 43.45 / 25.00, save, unsplit the 50.00 leg. Expect the parent at 73.45 with 'Amount left:' 50.00 — not 123.45, not 73.45. Unsplit the 43.45 leg too and expect no banner.
AC-5: in that same flow, confirm the surviving parent row still shows the payee under its split.
risks: The payee resolution rule — first promoted row carrying a payee, else the parent's — is new behaviour, not a repair of one line. On a split whose legs carry DIFFERENT payees and the first selected leg has one, the survivor takes the first, same as today; it differs only when an earlier promoted leg has none. I checked all five reachable shapes; a shape I did not think of would need the same check.

Recomputing the surviving parent's error changes a figure the register renders and a Distribute button acts on. The expense arm is covered by the browser flow; the income arm is unit-only, since I could not confirm the income route is distinguishable in the UI.

The keep-parent case is where F3, F4 and F8 land together, and it is the case most able to pass against a wrong fix: handing `updatedParentTransaction` straight to `recalculateSplit` yields a self-consistent-looking `difference: 7345`. AC-6 requires the red run per case so this cannot ship unverified.

Reviewer C's finding that the previous work order's AC-13 procedure cannot be performed as written (blanking a leg to 0.00 is not committable from the 'Add New' row) applies to how this is QA'd. AC-4 reaches the under-fill shape by unsplitting a leg from a correctly filled split rather than by committing an under-filled one. If QA finds that route is also unperformable, the criterion needs correcting — that is a plan change, not a code change.
The release note's `authors` field cannot be written until the committing account is known; conventions.md rejects `claude` and `github-actions` by identity denylist.
out_of_scope: F5 — the scope-bookkeeping finding about files PR #100's diff touched that its work order did not name. Both are comment-only, the PR is merged, and correcting a merged PR's work order is not a change any runtime can make. This order names every file it touches, including the release note the previous one omitted.

F9 — the previous work order's AC-13 test-verification procedure was not performable as written. That is a defect in the old plan's text, not in the code. This order avoids reproducing it (AC-2, AC-4) rather than editing a merged plan.
F8 as a separate item — the reviewer states the fix it asks for is the same test F3 asks for; the three-child keep-parent case covers both.

The `?? parentTransaction` degenerate path at :530. Reviewer A could not reach it: `Account.tsx:1242` passes every child and `:1266` is guarded by `selectedChildTransactions.length === 0 -> continue`. Rewriting a guard for an unreachable branch is the speculative change this repo's review history argues against.

A target length for the rewritten comment at :118-128, and the length policy itself. F6 is a review comment about a comment, and `.sdlc/memory/patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md` records exactly what specifying that prose produces. The comment is being rewritten because the expression under it changes, and it must describe the code as it now is; how many lines that takes is the implementer's call.

Whether the collapsed row's CATEGORY should also come from the leg rather than the parent. The collapse keeps the parent's category, which is right because the surviving row IS the parent, and unlike the payee a split's category is not moved down onto the children — so there is no parallel argument forcing it either way. Left alone rather than widening the diff.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: High on the three defects and on F7's disproof: I re-drove each against current main myself rather than taking the proposer's or the reviewer's word for it, and saw the exact wrong values — `payee: null` on the collapse, `payee: null` on the cleared leg, `difference: 12345` against an amount of 7345 — plus two live counterexamples to F7 (the #8207 parent keeps `payee-original`, and an edited split parent keeps `payee-EDITED`). I also confirmed the naive `recalculateSplit` remedy produces 7345 where the truth is 500, which is why edit (c) hands the helper the remaining children instead. I confirmed the existing 43 tests are green before any edit. What holds the number below the high band: two of the three rules are judgements rather than repairs — the collapsing leg's payee as the survivor's provenance, and hiding the banner on a balanced split — and neither is settled by anything in the code; the payee-cleared state is confirmed reachable through the reducer but not through the editor, so that leg rests on QA's AC-2 step; the release note's author field is a hard gate I cannot fill from here; and the new payee scan is new behaviour rather than a one-line fix, so a reachable shape neither the review nor I thought of would slip past. Every new test is required to have been seen red, which is where I would rather the review push than in the triage.
evidence: F1 reproduced on main by me. Driving the real `deleteTransaction` through `splitTransaction`: opened `{id:'p', amount:12345, payee:'payee-parent'}`, children c1=5000 / c2=7345; delete c1, then c2 -> `[{id:'p', is_parent:false, payee:null, amount:12345}]`. The leg being collapsed genuinely carried the payee; the survivor loses it.
F2 reproduced. `makeOpenedSplit` with c1 `{amount:5000, payee:null}` and c2 carrying the parent's payee, both unsplit -> survivor `{id:'p', amount:12345, payee:null, is_parent:false}`.

F3 and F4 reproduced. Three-child split `{id:'p', amount:12345, payee:'P'}`, children 5000/0/0, unsplit c1 -> parent `{amount:7345, payee:null, is_parent:true, error:{type:'SplitTransactionError', version:1, difference:12345}}` and promoted leg `{id:'c1', amount:5000, payee:'P', error:null}`. The amount moved; the error did not.

F4's remedy checked, not assumed. In this branch `parentTransaction` carries no `subtransactions` key at all, so `recalculateSplit(updatedParentTransaction)` measures against zero and reports `difference: 7345` where the truth is 500 on a 12345/5000/4345/2500 split with c1 promoted. Handing the same helper the REMAINING children instead returns 500 there, `null` when the remainder balances (12345 / 5000 / 4345 / 3000), 7345 on the all-zero-remainder fixture, and `null` on a balanced negative expense — so the helper is reusable and no signature needs to change.

F7 DISPROVEN, twice. `updateTransaction([{id:'q', payee:'payee-original'}], {id:'q', subtransactions:[two null-payee children]})` — the #8207 path — yields a parent at `payee:'payee-original'`, and unsplitting both legs returns `payee-original` purely through the parent fallback; F7's `payee: data.payee ?? null` returns null there. Separately, `updateTransaction(openedSplit, {id:'p', payee:'payee-EDITED'})` leaves the split parent at `payee:'payee-EDITED'`. A split parent does not always read `payee: null`.

Reachability checked for both payee sites. `Account.tsx:1242` passes every child and `:1266` is guarded by `selectedChildTransactions.length === 0 -> continue`, so the `newNonChildTransactions[0] ?? parentTransaction` degenerate path is not reachable from the app. `grep -rn 'is_parent: false' packages/` excluding tests returns transactions.ts:116 and :381 as the only constructors.

The user-visible surface confirmed: TransactionsTable.tsx:2350-2364 renders `error.difference` as 'Amount left:' behind `data-testid="transaction-error"` next to a `distribute-split-button`, and the mobile editor reads the same error. `recalculateSplit` is the only place that rule ('balanced means no error') is written, which is why edit (c) reuses it rather than restating it.
Baseline: `vitest --run src/shared/transactions.test.ts` on current main is 43/43 green before any edit, so a later failure is attributable.

All probes ran in packages/loot-core as scratch files `src/shared/__arbprobe*.test.ts`, all removed. `git status --short` shows only the untracked plan/ directory; nothing was committed, nothing was posted, and transactions.ts is byte-identical to its state on main.

alternatives_considered.approach: Apply F7 as written — drop the fallback to `payee: data.payee ?? null`, treating a split parent's payee as always null.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Disproven by probe, and it is a regression rather than a cleanup. `updateTransaction`'s #8207 path builds the new split parent by spreading `...transaction` over the plain row, which keeps the original payee; a split parent edited via `updateTransaction(txs, {id, payee})` also keeps it. On the #8207 shape the survivor returns `payee-original` through the parent fallback today and would return null under F7's line — the same class of bug AC-1 and AC-2 exist to close, reintroduced.

alternatives_considered.approach: Narrow the fallback to `data.payee === undefined ? parent.payee : data.payee`, which is reviewer A's first option for F2.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Correct that `??` treats an explicit null as absent, but it makes the wrong choice on the shape F2 is about: the survivor takes the cleared leg's explicit null and stays payee-less, which is the symptom. The reviewer's own second option — prefer the first promoted row that actually carries a payee — is the one that fixes it, and it subsumes the fallback.

alternatives_considered.approach: For F4, hand `updatedParentTransaction` to the existing `recalculateSplit`, or widen `SplitTransactionError` to take a difference directly and compute `newAmount - remainingTotal` by hand.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The first is silently wrong on any split whose remaining children are not all zero: I measured it reporting `difference: 7345` where the truth is 500, because the parent carries no `subtransactions` in this branch. The second is correct but restates a rule the module already states in one place and changes a shared signature to do it; passing the remaining children to the unchanged helper produces identical results on all four fixtures I checked. The proposal chose the second; I checked and it works, but the first-with-the-right-children is smaller and leaves no second definition of 'balanced means no error' to drift.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave F4 out of scope, as the reviewer suggested ('None required for this PR — worth a follow-up issue').
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This IS the follow-up issue, and the state is worse than 'stale': PR #100 made the surviving parent's amount non-zero where it used to be zero, so the banner now renders an 'Amount left:' that disagrees with the row, with a Distribute button wired to that number. Shipping F1 and F2 while leaving a wrong money figure on the adjacent branch fixes the loud half of one invariant.

alternatives_considered.approach: Take every finding at face value, including the comment-length trim as its own change with a specified length and the scope-bookkeeping finding as work.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: F5 is bookkeeping on a merged PR, not a defect, and patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md is the recorded shape of that mistake. F9 is a defect in the previous work order's text, not in the code; this order avoids repeating it rather than editing the old plan. The comment is being rewritten regardless because the expression under it changes, and it has to stop asserting that a split parent's payee is always null — but specifying how many lines it should be is transcribing a review comment into an acceptance criterion, which is what that pattern file warns produces.

assumptions: A split leg's payee can be explicitly null while the split is intact. Reproduced by driving `makeOpenedSplit` with `{id:'c1', payee: null}` and confirmed that `updateTransaction(txs, {id:'c1', payee:null})` on the real reducer returns a cleared leg; whether the editor lets a user save that is QA's AC-2 step, not something I drove.

Reading the payee off the collapsing leg in `deleteTransaction` is the right provenance. The alternative — that deleting a leg should leave the survivor payee-less — has no support in the code, and the row's amount is the whole split's, so the split's payee belongs on it. A judgement, not something I proved.

For the surviving-parent error, `remainingChildTransactions` is exactly the set of children still behind the parent. It follows from the branch's own arithmetic — the parent is kept only when at least two children remain, and `promotedTotal` is a subtraction against that same set — but I did not exercise the DB write path to confirm the surviving children are untouched by it.

Both changes belong in one release note rather than two: one user-visible story, and the conventions file requires exactly one body line per note, so splitting would mean two one-line notes for one bugfix.
unknowns: Whether the 'Amount left:' banner should render at all for a parent whose remainder balances its new amount. Edit (c) sets `error: null` in that case, hiding the banner and both its buttons. That follows the rule `recalculateSplit` already states, but no test or review comment in this issue says the banner is wanted on a balanced split.

Whether F2's cleared-leg state is reachable from the editor rather than only from the reducer. The reducer accepts it, which is what the reviewer reported and what I reproduced; whether the UI lets a user commit it is unverified.

Whether `makeTransactionWithChildCategory`'s `data.payee` becomes unused after edit (b). The plan keeps `data` for `category`, which is still read off the promoted row, so the parameter stays used and the signature does not change.
validated_work_order.debate_summary:
There was no critique to judge: `plan/critique.json` is empty (`{}`), so round 2 produced nothing and every judgement below is mine, made against the code and by re-running the probes. I largely kept the proposal's triage — it is unusually well evidenced, and I confirmed its four behavioural claims and its disproof of F7 independently rather than taking them on trust — but I changed the plan in three places.

First, and largest: the proposal is right that F4's obvious remedy is wrong and wrong that the existing helper is therefore unusable. It measured `recalculateSplit` against the stale parent and concluded helper reuse was off the table, then planned to widen `SplitTransactionError` to take a difference directly. I checked: the parent in that branch carries no `subtransactions` at all, which is exactly why the naive call reports 7345 — but handing the same helper the REMAINING children returns 500 / null / 7345 / null on the four fixtures, identical to the hand-rolled arithmetic. So I dropped the signature change. That is one fewer edit to a shared type and one fewer definition of 'balanced means no error' to drift out of step with `recalculateSplit`. I am recording this as a correction rather than a refutation: the proposal's diagnosis was right and its arithmetic was right; only its conclusion about the helper was wrong, and it reached it without testing the alternative.

Second, I refused the comment-length target. The proposal's files[] says 'cut to roughly three lines', which is an acceptance criterion about the diff rather than about behaviour, and patterns/planner-read-comment-wording-as-the-defect.md records in this repository exactly what that produces — a string of near-identical PRs that change no executable statement. The comment is being rewritten regardless because the expression beneath it changes, and it must stop claiming the parent's payee is always null, since this work disproves that. What it says and how long it is stays the implementer's call. The proposal treated F6 as cheap because it folded the rewrite into an edit it was making anyway; the fold is fine, the length target is not, and the two should not be confused.

Third, I dropped the proposal's route_request, which asked for `scope_changed` at stage `plan` while saying in the same field that nothing was requested. Its substantive point — that the router's 'two live product defects' framing understates the work — is fair and is recorded in `risks` instead. The route itself (plan -> implement -> review -> qa) is right for this: the defects reproduce deterministically in the reducer with no browser, and review is exactly the check a novel money rule on a branch with three hand-applied variants needs. No stage is missing.

Where I agree with the proposal and expect pushback: F1 and F2 are the same defect at two sites and I have kept them as two edits, because they are two sites and the second is only safe once the first is understood. And I agree with it that F5 and F9 are not code work — but I want that on the record as a judgement, not a fact: F5 is bookkeeping on a merged PR, which is true, and F9 is a real defect in the previous order's AC-13 text, which is also true and which this order sidesteps by writing AC-2 and AC-4 to be performable rather than by editing anything.
residual_risks: Edit (c) is asserted by unit tests on four fixtures and by one browser flow (the expense arm). The income arm of the same branch is unit-only — go there first if a browser check disagrees with the unit expectation.
